the optimization of the CMS Outer tracker for the HL L HC.
the development and characterization of silicon sensors for the HL L HC.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for a sensor with a thickness of 100-200 m, a high resistivity bulk is preferred.
the best compromise between radiation hardness and sensor performance can be achieved with the combination of high resistivity (HR) bulk material and a thickness of 300 m.

the best choice of silicon bulk material and sensor thickness for the CMS Outer Tracker depends on the position in the tracker, and that the best option is a combination of two different silicon bulk materials and sensor thicknesses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 300 μm thick n-in-p sensors have the best performance in terms of radiation hardness and charge collection, and are the most promising candidates for the upgrade.
for the HL LHV, the best performance is achieved with the 100 μm thick sensors made out of high resistive n-type float zone silicon.
the best performance for the HL LHV CMS Outer Tracker is achieved with 200 m thick n-on-p silicon sensors produced with the planar process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of silicon bulk material and sensor thickness has a significant effect on the radiation tolerance of the devices.
the radiation hardness of silicon bulk material is the most important factor in determining sensor performance after irradiation.
the performance of the sensors is very sensitive to the bulk material and that the choice of bulk material should be based on the expected radiation level.
